Prediction Object for Change Point Detection

Source: R/PredictionCpt.R
PredictionCpt.Rd

This object wraps the predictions returned by a learner of class LearnerCpt, i.e. the predicted penalty log(lambda) for each sequence. It is the bridge from a LearnerCpt to a measure: $score() compares the predicted penalties against the true label regions stored in $truth.

The task_type is set to "changepoint".

Super class

mlr3::Prediction -> PredictionCpt

Active bindings

response

(numeric())
Access the stored predicted penalty log(lambda). Returns NA for observations without a stored prediction.

Method new()

Creates a new instance of this R6 class.

Usage

PredictionCpt$new(
  task = NULL,
  row_ids = task$row_ids,
  truth = task$truth(row_ids),
  response = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  check = TRUE,
  extra = NULL,
  raw = NULL
)

Arguments

task

(TaskCpt)
Task, used to extract defaults for row_ids and truth.

row_ids

(integer())
Row ids of the predicted observations, i.e. the row ids of the test set.

truth

(list() of data.table::data.table())
True label regions, one data.table(start, end, label) per observation.

response

(numeric())
Predicted penalty log(lambda). One element for each observation in the test set.

weights

(numeric())
Measure weights, one for each observation in the test set. Constructed from the weights_measure column of the TaskCpt, if present.

check

(logical(1))
If TRUE, performs some argument checks and predict type conversions.

extra

(list())
Named list of extra data to store alongside the predictions. Each element must have one entry per observation in the test set.

raw

(any)
Raw prediction object from the upstream model. Stored as-is, without validation.

Method clone()

The objects of this class are cloneable with this method.

deep

Whether to make a deep clone.

Examples

library(data.table)
#> 
#> Attaching package: ‘data.table’
#> The following object is masked from ‘package:base’:
#> 
#>     %notin%
set.seed(36)
toy = data.table(
  seq = list(c(rnorm(100, 18), rnorm(100, 36), rnorm(100, 9)), rnorm(100, 0)),
  label = list(
    data.table(start = c(90, 190), end = c(110, 210), label = c("1change", "1change")),
    data.table(start = 1, end = 100, label = "0changes")
  )
)
task = TaskCpt$new(
  id = "toy", backend = toy,
  target = "label", sequence = "seq", label_type = "changepoint"
)

p = PredictionCpt$new(task = task, response = c(2.5, 3.0))
p
#> 
#> ── <PredictionCpt> for 2 observations: ─────────────────────────────────────────
#>  row_ids             truth response
#>        1 <data.table[2x3]>      2.5
#>        2 <data.table[1x3]>      3.0
p$response
#> [1] 2.5 3.0
as.data.table(p)
#>    row_ids             truth response
#>      <int>            <list>    <num>
#> 1:       1 <data.table[2x3]>      2.5
#> 2:       2 <data.table[1x3]>      3.0
